rationale: The assistant gave the correct core answer immediately: 'No, you must stop using it immediately', explained the moisture/live-parts shock risk, and referred to a qualified engineer to replace the glass top or whole unit, which matches the ground truth. It omitted telling her to isolate the hob at the cooker switch or consumer unit even though the hob remains energised and spilled water may have entered, and asked no follow-up about model number or home insurance, both of which would have been useful. The replacement recommendation is appropriately conditioned on engineer assessment with no compatibility claims, and nothing was fabricated.
